practiceBoundaries: 22 named formation, 22 interpretation and four bounded contextual selections are not an unrestricted production assessment.

Two shared talking contexts accept について, に関して and のことを, with four substantive extra buttons in total. Their stylistic/structural differences are explained, not independently graded by these shared tasks.

Repeated or closely paired scenes share example keys across facets, including evaluative transfers, speech treatment and nominalization/layer questions. Forty-eight tasks are not forty-eight independent discourse situations.
Case attachment practices nouns, ordinary な-adjectives and two plain verbs. The article's i-adjective example is supporting recognition, not a separately practiced facet.

Added は/も, nonhuman evaluators, にとって plus adjective noun modification, nominalized complements of に対する, and the full purpose/cause range are article support or linked follow-up, not independent new facets.
Comparison recognizes two verb-clause situations and the nominalizer/relation layers. Broader noun/adjective comparative formation and further compound relations are deferred.

Six core formation blanks now include the supplied noun and its relation; two nominalization blanks include a transformed plain verb and こと. These remain bounded scaffolded operations, not unrestricted productive fluency.

basis: The three opening relations are distinguished by complete sentences, not English-preposition matching. Directed treatment is not equated with hostility; evaluation is not equated with intended or achieved benefit.
Noun modification distinguishes についての, に対する/に対しての and に関する/に関しての. Simple に and verb-specific argument patterns are preserved rather than globally replaced.

The formal-noun bridge adequately answers this lesson's bounded question: Nのこと is an object noun phrase, Nであること nominalizes a predicate, ため/場合 have construction-dependent attachment, and a nominalized clause can precede the outer relation.

The comparison use of のに対して is separated from a directed target and from concessive のに. The article explicitly limits comparative attachment practice rather than pretending to teach its entire paradigm.

Register claims are tendencies. Shared subject-matter descriptions are not forced into artificial mutually exclusive categories. Kana and recognized kanji spellings are distinguished without asserting equal frequency.

Readings, translations, bracketed structural explanations and relevant prerequisite links make the article accessible within the stated series. No additional catalogue of formal nouns or compound expressions is necessary for this scope.
articleVerdicts.qualification: CLEAN means no actionable article defect established in this frozen scope, not exhaustive certainty about every possible context or grammatical analysis.

exerciseVerdicts.correctnessBasis: No incorrect completed Japanese construction, consequential mistranslation, unfair answer rejection within the visible bounded task, unsupported accepted rendering, incorrect wrong-option rationale, or contextual vocabulary mapping was established. practiceAssessment.area: Shared subject matter and Nのこと
practiceAssessment.actualPractice: Two bounded shared-answer tasks, two object-particle completions and two interpretations. All three shared formulations fit the teacher and plan scenes; the shared tasks do not independently test register selection or generation of each alternative.

Two intended-benefit interpretations, two bounded selections of にとって and two directed-treatment interpretations. The two standpoint selections distinguish among the three named core relations; they do not themselves ask learners to choose between にとって and のために.
Two noun-link, two な-adjective-link and two polite-to-plain verb completions. I-adjective attachment is explained in the article but is not separately elicited by this set.

Two explicitly requested こと completions, four Nであること/Nのこと interpretations, two comparisons, two identifications of nominalizing の and two identifications of the outer について. Comparative connector production and broader こと/の distribution are not tested.

The 132 lexical spans supply ordinary words and correct displayed readings; the 219 exclusions protect grammatical targets, function material and punctuation. No lexical-span leak of a hidden target was found. CR-F01 concerns the task instructions, not the vocabulary layer.

findings.title: Every interpretation instruction lists its correct answer first
exactClaimAndEvidence: The first label after 'Use these operational answer labels outside the quotation:' is the keyed answer in all 18 definition-list interpretation tasks.

At line 2820, the being-a-student task lists 状態 before 関連. At line 2870, the matters-about-students task reverses that list to 関連 before 状態. The order follows the answer rather than a stable explanatory ordering.
The remaining four interpretation tasks also put the answer first: 'Answer の or に対して' at lines 3111 and 3287; 'Answer について or こと' at lines 3372 and 3431.
A read-only comparison of all 22 instructions with their acceptedAnswers verified the pattern; this is not an inference from the serialized options array.
findings.learningImpact: A learner can obtain every interpretation answer by copying the first listed label without interpreting the Japanese construction. Shuffling quiz buttons would not remove the cue in the instruction text. This affects the diagnostic value of interpretation practice, not the grammatical truth of the answers.
findings.minimalRecommendedRemedy: Use an answer-independent stable order for each comparable label set, or otherwise counterbalance the instruction lists independently of the keyed answer. Preserve the explicit definitions, readings and outside-the-quotation instruction. No unrestricted-production redesign is needed.

sourceEvidence.explanation: The paired instruction text and answer keys directly establish the cue. An external linguistic rule is not needed for this editorial/assessment finding.

findings.scopeQualification: This finding is not an objection to naming a construction in a formation drill. It concerns an unintended positional answer code in tasks explicitly asking for interpretation.

optionalObservations.title: Example keys do not consistently identify repeated underlying contexts
optionalObservations.observation: The 旅行について話しました interpretation and formation use trip-topic versus trip-form; the 家族のために働きます interpretation and attachment task use family-benefit versus family-noun-link. The history-book tasks also describe reading a history book under different connector-family instructions but use different keys. Other interpretation/formation pairs correctly reuse a key.
optionalObservations.impact: This does not make a Japanese answer wrong. It does mean neither 48 tasks nor 38 distinct keys is a defensible count of independent discourse contexts.
optionalObservations.optionalRemedy: If these keys are intended to identify shared semantic contexts, consider aligning these additional pairs. If they are intentionally task-family-specific, document that narrower meaning and do not report key counts as independent contextual breadth.
optionalObservations.confidence: high for the observed duplication; conditional on the intended downstream semantics for whether metadata changes are desirable

optionalObservations.title: Distinguish highly scaffolded copying from productive attachment practice
optionalObservations.observation: These eight formation instructions print the exact kana or kanji connector/nominalizer that must be copied into the blank. They can reinforce a supplied model and its location, but success does not independently demonstrate selection or productive formation. This is different from the noun-modifier and polite-to-plain tasks, which require an actual structural operation.
optionalObservations.optionalRemedy: Keep the named-form restriction if desired. For stronger diagnostic practice, make some items discriminate a correct attachment from an erroneous extra の or require a small transformation within that same named family. Alternatively, retain them as explicitly scaffolded rehearsal and avoid treating them as evidence of independent mastery.
optionalObservations.nonblockingReason: The article openly distinguishes named-form practice from bounded selection, and the set also contains genuine structural and interpretive tasks. Unrestricted production is not required.

basis: The three opening relations are distinguished by complete sentences, not English-preposition matching. Directed treatment is not equated with hostility; evaluation is not equated with intended or achieved benefit.
Noun modification distinguishes についての, に対する/に対しての and に関する/に関しての. Simple に and verb-specific argument patterns are preserved rather than globally replaced.

The formal-noun bridge adequately answers this lesson's bounded question: Nのこと is an object noun phrase, Nであること nominalizes a predicate, ため/場合 have construction-dependent attachment, and a nominalized clause can precede the outer relation.

The comparison use of のに対して is separated from a directed target and from concessive のに. The article explicitly limits comparative attachment practice rather than pretending to teach its entire paradigm.

Register claims are tendencies. Shared subject-matter descriptions are not forced into artificial mutually exclusive categories. Kana and recognized kanji spellings are distinguished without asserting equal frequency.

Readings, translations, bracketed structural explanations and relevant prerequisite links make the article accessible within the stated series. No additional catalogue of formal nouns or compound expressions is necessary for this scope.

Six named-family noun-modifying completions, including the necessary の and both taught 対する/関する realizations. This is a legitimate structural skill despite the named-family restriction.

practiceAssessment.actualPractice: Two bounded shared-answer tasks, two object-particle completions and two interpretations. All three shared formulations fit the teacher and plan scenes; the shared tasks do not independently test register selection or generation of each alternative.

Two intended-benefit interpretations, two bounded selections of にとって and two directed-treatment interpretations. The two standpoint selections distinguish among the three named core relations; they do not themselves ask learners to choose between にとって and のために.
Two noun-link, two な-adjective-link and two polite-to-plain verb completions. I-adjective attachment is explained in the article but is not separately elicited by this set.

Two explicitly requested こと completions, four Nであること/Nのこと interpretations, two comparisons, two identifications of nominalizing の and two identifications of the outer について. Comparative connector production and broader こと/の distribution are not tested.

The 132 lexical spans supply ordinary words and correct displayed readings; the 219 exclusions protect grammatical targets, function material and punctuation. No lexical-span leak of a hidden target was found. CR-F01 concerns the task instructions, not the vocabulary layer.
